draft.title: Organisational structures
card: An organisational structure shows who reports to whom in a business. It sets out the levels of authority from the top down.
a structure with many levels of managers. Each manager oversees a small team, and instructions pass down through each level.
a structure with few levels of managers, also called horizontal. Each manager oversees more workers, so decisions can be quicker and workers often have more say.
A vertical structure gives close supervision but can slow decisions, as a request may pass through many levels. A flat structure gives workers more freedom, but each manager has more people to lead.
draft.remember: Many levels means vertical. Few levels means flat, with quicker decisions.

a.q: Which description fits a flat organisational structure?
opts: Few levels of managers and more say for workers
Many levels of managers and close supervision
Many levels of managers and slower decisions
Few levels of managers and no workers with a say
a.why: A flat structure has few levels of managers, so workers often have more say. The second and third options describe a vertical structure. The last is wrong because a flat structure usually gives workers more say, not none.

b.q: Tran's bakery in Hobart has 6 staff and one owner. Orders from customers need quick answers, and bakers suggest new recipes. Which structure suits it best, and why?
opts: Flat, because decisions can be made quickly
Vertical, because decisions can be made quickly
Flat, because every request passes through many managers
Vertical, because bakers need more say in decisions
b.why: A small team that needs quick decisions and ideas from workers suits a flat structure, which has few levels. A vertical structure is tempting because it sounds well organised, but it passes requests through many levels and slows decisions.
b.clue: Think about how many managers a request must pass through.

a.best: Few levels of managers and more say for workers

b.best: Flat, because decisions can be made quickly

problems.detail: Why (a) refers to options by position ('the second and third options', 'the last'), but the options are shuffled. In the order shown, the first and second describe a vertical structure, the third is 'no workers with a say', and the last is the correct answer. The why contradicts the options a student sees.
The remember line says 'Few levels means flat, with quicker decisions', which states quicker decisions as certain. The card only says decisions 'can be quicker'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer and the card is accurate. However, why (a) names options by position, which does not match the shuffled order, and the remember line drops the card's 'can' about quicker decisions.
